The PowerNV L0 currently pushes the OS xive context when running a vCPU
regardless of whether it is running a nested guest. The problem is that
xive OS ring interrupts will be delivered while the L2 is running.
At the moment
column3: the L2 guest runs with LPCR[LPES]=0

column1: actually makes external interrupts go to the L0. That causes the L2 to
exit and the interrupt taken or injected into the L1
respects this behaves like an escalation. It's not clear if this was
deliberate or not
column2: there's no comment about it and the L1 is actually

column1: allowed to clear LPES in the L2
When the L2 is running
column2: the L1 is essentially in a ceded state with

column1: respect to external interrupts (it can't respond to them directly and
won't get scheduled again absent some additional event). So the natural
way to solve this is when the L0 handles a H_ENTER_NESTED hypercall to
run the L2
column2: have it arm the escalation interrupt and don't push the L1

column1: context while running the L2.
